summary:
Dagestan is a republic within the Russian Federation and stands under the national framework set out in Russia's own record; that layer is not restated here.

The UK Home Office country policy note on sexual orientation and gender identity and expression, version 2.0 of June 2025, names the North Caucasus, Dagestan among them, as an area where LGBT+ people are likely to face treatment amounting to persecution. The note documents systematic campaigns by Chechen and North Caucasus authorities between 2017 and 2024 involving abduction, torture and extrajudicial killings, and assesses trans people and visible advocates specifically as at risk. The most recent documented instance of such a campaign in this record is from 2024; no later instance is documented.

Global Affairs Canada advises against all travel to Russia. Its advisory flags frequent terrorist attacks in the republics of Chechnya, Dagestan, Ingushetia and Stavropol Krai, and states that entry to certain areas and regions requires special permission from the Ministry of the Interior. The same advisory warns of violence targeting 2SLGBTQI+ persons, and names the North Caucasus republics of Chechnya and Dagestan in particular.

David Isteev of North Caucasus SOS, who works in exile, told the Human Rights House Foundation that there is no safe life for LGBTIQ+ people in the North Caucasus and that even private existence can trigger violence, detention or forced return to families. He said the situation worsens year on year.
tangentialFactors:
Two foreign governments single out this republic alongside Chechnya rather than treating the North Caucasus as indistinguishable from the rest of Russia: the UK Home Office persecution assessment and the Canadian travel advisory both name Dagestan explicitly, which places the republic above the national baseline described in the parent record.

Terrorism risk is documented for Dagestan independently of LGBT-related risk and affects movement within the republic; the Canadian advisory couples it with a special-permission requirement from the Ministry of the Interior for entry to certain areas and regions.

The documented pattern of abductions, torture and extrajudicial killings runs across the North Caucasus as a subregional phenomenon from 2017 to 2024, with Chechnya the most heavily documented case; whether Dagestan-specific incidents are recorded separately from the Chechen cases is unresolved in these sources.
localsOnly:
North Caucasus SOS reports that for LGBTIQ+ residents of the subregion, private existence itself can expose people to violence, detention or forced return to their families, and that the organisation's staff work in exile rather than locally. David Isteev of North Caucasus SOS stated to the Human Rights House Foundation that the situation worsens year on year.

Residents moving between republics must account for the Ministry of the Interior special-permission requirement for entry to certain areas and regions, alongside the general terrorism risk recorded for Dagestan.
outOfScopeNotes:
No Dagestan-specific statute, court decision, or dated incident involving a trans person appears in this inventory; the republic-level findings rest on two foreign-government assessments and one activist interview, and the underlying incident documentation is not broken down by republic in these sources.

Whether the 2017 to 2024 campaigns attributed to North Caucasus authorities include Dagestan-specific cases with their own dates and outcomes, separately from the Chechen cases, is unresolved here.

No trans-specific violence figure with a denominator exists for Dagestan in this inventory, so no comparison with the republic's general homicide rate can be made.

The ILGA-Europe 2026 score of 2% is a figure for Russia as a whole and is carried by the national record rather than treated as a Dagestan measurement.
